description: Three-panel composite figure of secondary-electron SEM micrographs of a medium-manganese low-density steel after three annealing treatments. All panels were acquired with an ETD detector at 20.00 kV, spot 5.9, mode Custom, magnification 3,000 x, and each carries a 40 µm scale bar at bottom right; WD is 10.0 mm in (a) and 10.7 mm in (b) and (c). (a) shows dark, flat, smooth regions traversed by a discontinuous bright, rough-etched network. (b) shows a markedly denser, more continuous bright network enclosing smaller dark areas. (c) shows predominantly smooth dark matrix with only sparse bright network remnants. The caption identifies (a) as AN750, (b) as AN800 and (c) again as "AN800" (almost certainly a typographical error for AN850, since the citing text discusses AN750/AN800/AN850). The bright network is the bainitic constituent and the dark smooth regions the ferrite: the citing text reports ferrite volume fractions of 52 %, 43 % and 69 % with average grain sizes of 5.7, 5.4 and 6.8 µm, and bainite fractions of 43.0 %, 55.1 % and 30.8 % (3.0, 4.1, 2.6 µm) for AN750, AN800 and AN850. No numeric composition or property values are printed on the micrographs.

subfigures.description: Secondary-electron SEM micrograph (ETD, 20.00 kV, spot 5.9, 3,000 x, WD 10.0 mm, 40 µm scale bar) showing dark flat ferrite regions crossed by a discontinuous bright, rough-etched network; caption labels it AN750.

Secondary-electron SEM micrograph of the same type and magnification (WD 10.7 mm, 40 µm scale bar) in which the bright rough network is denser and more continuous, enclosing smaller dark ferrite areas; caption labels it AN800.

Secondary-electron SEM micrograph (WD 10.7 mm, 40 µm scale bar) dominated by smooth dark matrix with only sparse bright network regions; the caption labels it AN800, but the citing text implies this should be AN850.

observations.observation: All three panels are secondary-electron SEM micrographs recorded at 20.00 kV, spot 5.9, ETD detector, mode Custom, magnification 3,000 x, each with a 40 µm scale bar printed in the instrument info strip.
Working distance is 10.0 mm in panel (a) and 10.7 mm in panels (b) and (c).

Panel (a) shows a discontinuous bright, rough-etched network embedded in dark smooth matrix; the network is denser and more continuous in (b), while in (c) the smooth dark matrix dominates with only sparse bright network regions.
The caption labels the panels AN750, AN800 and AN800, so the third panel's label is inconsistent with the AN750/AN800/AN850 set discussed in the citing text.
The caption states the figure shows SEM morphology of AN750, AN800 and AN850 samples.
The citing text states ferrite volume fractions of 52 %, 43 % and 69 % for the AN750, AN800 and AN850 specimens respectively.
The citing text states average ferrite grain sizes of 5.7 µm, 5.4 µm and 6.8 µm for AN750, AN800 and AN850.
The citing text states bainite volume fractions of 43.0 %, 55.1 % and 30.8 % with average grain sizes of 3.0 µm, 4.1 µm and 2.6 µm for AN750, AN800 and AN850.
The citing text states that grain refinement strengthening contributions were 264 MPa, 256 MPa and 292 MPa for the AN750, AN800 and AN850 specimens.
The citing text states that retained austenite content was less than 5 %, so its strengthening contribution was neglected.

The citing text states that ferrite grain size and volume fraction were statistically analysed with Image-Pro Plus software on several SEM images per specimen group, with average values reported as Fig. 13.
No numeric values, phase annotations or grain-size labels are printed directly on the micrographs themselves.

unreadable_items: The bright and dark microstructural constituents are not annotated on the micrographs, so ferrite/bainite assignment cannot be confirmed from pixels alone
Small text in the instrument info strip other than the numeric fields (e.g. the bottom-right 'Univ' logo) is only partially readable
Panel (c) caption label reads 'AN800', which conflicts with the AN850 sample discussed in the citing text; the correct sample identity of (c) is not resolvable from the image
